units.selection_reason: For intersections of quadrics, a familiar commutative parameter curve accounts for a categorical component only in special low-dimensional cases. The source constructs the quadratic dual Clifford algebra, sheafifies an even subalgebra over the parameter space, and uses its module category as the persistent component. When ambient dimension exceeds twice the number of equations, exceptional objects form the complement; at equality, the noncommutative component is the entire category. The generic move is to preserve a dual description by widening from spaces to sheaves of algebras when commutative geometry no longer suffices.
